evals.name: Context Token Cost
evals.formula: 100 · clamp((6000 − T) / 5400) per pattern; T = min(tokens of API+Config+Enum+Interface files, tokens of a ≥80%-complete manifest card)
evals.summary: mean 438 tok/pattern (33 via cards); benchmark median 912
evals.scope: Per pattern: tokens an agent must read to use it (its manifest card when ≥ 80 % complete, else the API + config + enum + interface files). CSS-only components have no TypeScript contract.
advice: Mean 438 tokens per pattern via cards, against 2749 from source; benchmark median 912.
Every pattern is served by its manifest card; keep cards complete so this holds.
The compiled .d.ts is 53k tokens: agents must load a card, never the whole typing file.

evals.name: Prop Surface & Typing Precision
evals.formula: 100 · (0.4·clamp(1 − max(0, props − 8)/12) + 0.6·precise/props); precise = boolean | number | enum/union | typed object/array | free string; a string validated with validateInRange or defaulted to an enum member is a stringly-typed enum (imprecise)
evals.scope: Per pattern: how many config props it has and how many are precisely typed. CSS-only components have no props.
advice: 7 stringly-typed enums remain: DatePicker.TimeFormat, AccordionItem.Icon, AccordionItem.IconPosition, Notification.Position, Notification.Width, Sidebar.Width, Tabs.Height. Turning them into validated enum types changes runtime fallback behaviour (B-9).

Patterns over the free allowance of 8 props: DatePicker (18), RangeSlider (15), Dropdown (12), TimePicker (12), Carousel (11), MonthPicker (10) +1 more; splitting or grouping props is a public-contract change.

evals.name: Machine-Readable Schema Completeness
evals.formula: mean over manifest entries of the mean of six facets (props typed, defaults, api, events, cssClasses, markup) · 100 · (entries / patterns); 0 without docs-ai/osui.components.json
evals.summary: 33/33 patterns in manifest; facet means props 100, defaults 100, api 100, events 100, cssClasses 100, markup 100
evals.scope: Per pattern: how complete its entry in docs-ai/osui.components.json is across six facets. CSS-only components are documented in llms-patterns.txt instead.
advice: 33/33 patterns in the manifest; facet means props 100, defaults 100, api 100, events 100, cssClasses 100, markup 100.
Keep it at 100 by running npm run docs:ai in every PR that touches a pattern; the CI freshness check fails a stale commit.

evals.name: Type Strictness
evals.formula: 100 − min(40, 4·implicitAny/KLOC) − min(20, 10·explicitAny/KLOC) − min(10, 2.5·suppressions) − 30·(exported public functions without return type / total)
evals.summary: 0 implicit-any findings, 0 explicit any, 0 ts-ignore/expect-error, 0/422 public fns without return type (43.6 KLOC)
evals.scope: Measured per file over the whole program (implicit any, explicit any, suppressions, return types), so it has no per-component cell.
advice: 0 implicit-any, 0 explicit any, 0 suppressions, 0/422 public functions without a return type over 43.6 KLOC; noImplicitAny is on.
Next step of this kind: strictNullChecks, which is a larger behaviour-neutral annotation pass.

evals.name: Documentation Coverage
evals.formula: 35·(API functions with description + @param per parameter) + 15·(config props with a comment) + 0.5·agentDocs; agentDocs = 25·llms.txt + 25·llms-components coverage + 25·llms-tokens.txt + 25·llms-patterns.txt
evals.summary: API JSDoc 348/348, prop comments 141/141, agent docs 100/100
evals.scope: Per pattern: API functions and config props with documentation (cell = documented share). CSS-only components have no API.
advice: API JSDoc 348/348, prop comments 141/141, agent docs 100/100
Coverage is complete; the generator reads the same JSDoc, so new functions and props need a comment before docs-ai regenerates.

evals.name: Public API Shape Consistency
evals.formula: 100 · (0.4·canonical members present/7 + 0.3·non-lifecycle functions returning the CreateApiResponse envelope + 0.2·camelCase parameters + 0.1·no inline error-code literals)
evals.summary: 0 missing canonical members, 6 functions without envelope, 0 non-camelCase params
evals.scope: Per pattern: canonical API members present, functions returning the response envelope, camelCase parameters. CSS-only components have no API.
advice: 6 functions return void instead of the response envelope: SwipeEvents.Dispose, SwipeEvents.RegisterCallback, SwipeEvents.GestureMove, SwipeEvents.GestureEnd, TouchEvents.Dispose, TouchEvents.RegisterCallback. Wrapping them changes error propagation (B-3).
0 missing canonical members, 0 non-camelCase parameters.

evals.name: Markup Contract Depth
evals.formula: 100 − 20·max(0, depth − 3) − 4·max(0, distinct elements − 6); measured on the deepest HTML template of the component's story; distinct = unique tag+classes signatures (repeated items count once)
evals.summary: 81 components measured; mean depth 3.7, max 8; 22 without story
evals.scope: Per component: depth and distinct parts of the deepest HTML template in its Storybook story. Components without a story cannot be measured.
advice: 22 components have no story: add one HTML template each to measure them.

Deepest contracts: lightbox-image (depth 8, 22 parts), master-detail (depth 7, 10 parts), Sidebar (depth 6, 12 parts), bottom-bar-item (depth 7, 6 parts), Dropdown (depth 6, 10 parts), dropdown (depth 6, 10 parts) +19 more. Flattening them is a DOM-contract change (B-5).

evals.name: Design Token Semantics
evals.formula: per component SCSS (compiled): 100 · (0.55·(1 − hardcoded/themeable) + 0.30·(reads via --osui-* API/themeable) + 0.15·clamp(1 − !important/(2% of themeable)))
evals.scope: Per component SCSS: themeable declarations that are hardcoded, routed through --osui-* knobs, or read a token. Files with nothing themeable cannot be scored.
advice: 561 of 3074 themeable declarations (18 %) read through --osui-* knobs; 95 hardcoded; 10 !important.

Lowest knob routing: bulk-actions (0/11), form (0/18), scrollable-area (0/12), menu-layout-native (0/11), ButtonLoading (0/11), Dropdown (0/10). Routing is additive when the knob default equals the current value, except for portaled elements (B-7).

evals.name: CSS Selector Complexity
evals.formula: per component SCSS (compiled): 100 · (0.6·clamp(1 − max(0, mean combinators − 1)/3) + 0.4·clamp(1 − max(0, p90 class-specificity − 2)/4))
evals.summary: 3081 selectors in 99 files; mean depth 0.9, 212 selectors with ≥3 combinators
evals.scope: Per component SCSS: mean combinators per selector and the p90 class specificity. Files with no rules cannot be scored.
advice: 3081 selectors in 99 files; mean depth 0.9, 212 selectors with ≥3 combinators

Highest specificity: Rating (p90 6, max 6), Accordion (p90 7, max 4), header-layout-side (p90 6, max 3), menu-layout-native (p90 8, max 3), list-item (p90 6, max 4), form (p90 8, max 4). Flattening into state classes changes cascade order for existing overrides (B-6).

evals.name: Composition Model & Standards Alignment
evals.formula: 100 − 12·max(0, inheritance depth − 1) − 5·max(0, contract files − 4) − 15·(configs accepted only as JSON string) − 10·(event names typed as string) − 15·(global namespaces instead of ES modules)
evals.summary: mean inheritance depth 1.8, mean 7.4 contract files; 0 JSON-string-only Create, 33 global-namespace APIs
evals.scope: Per pattern: inheritance depth, contract files, typed configs and events, module format. CSS-only components have no classes.
advice: Mean inheritance depth 1.8 (max 4), mean 7.4 contract files; 0 JSON-string-only Create, 2 string event names, 33 global-namespace APIs.
Configs and events are typed additively (S-9). The remaining cost is the AMD global namespace and provider inheritance chains, which need the ES-module facade (B-4).
